'Alt Chain Path' or alternate chains are meant to be used in conjunction with specific parts enable settings.
As an example, let's say you have an outfit with hard armor plate around the breast area.
Then, with parts enable you want to remove that armor plate and now it's bare tits.
 Well, obviously there would be a difference in breast jiggle between the two.
You can use two different chain files with extra outfits.
One will be used with a certain combonation of parts enable settings.
The alternate will be used if any of the desginated 'False for EO Alt Chain Usage' (EO meaning extra outfits)
parts enabled checkboxes are set unchecked/false.

'Enable Mesh Parts on Preset Switch?' is meant to change the way parts enable is handled upon changing the preset.
The default behavior is to respect override parts enabled on preset switches.
However, sometimes you might want parts to be re-enabled first if you are switching
to a different preset with override parts enabled unchecked.
The behavior you have set will be preset specific and affect both manual switching and autoswitching of presets.
The behavior when checked enables all mesh parts and then applies your PE preset settings.
Keep in mind, the setting to enable all first has the potential drawback to
set parts enabled that would otherwise be disabled by the game, hence why 'Override Parts Enabled?' is even an option in the first place.

'OutfitJcnsPath' (This has a special parsing structure.
You can use as many Jcns files as you want, just be sure to include a suffix for each individual entry.
(example: 'OutfitJcnsPath1', 'OutfitJcnsPath2')
The value for these entries also have a special parsing structure.
An example being 'MyOutfitMod\JointConstraintsFile.jcns(true)((2))(((1.0)))'
This can be broken down into path (string), enable update timing override (boolean),
update timing mode (int between 0-3), blend rate (System.Single).
More info for what these are set to is displayed within the EO information.

For 'List Current Character Scales', these are scales that are applied to the characters in-game.
So for the files you work with out of the game inside Blender,
it's possible they will be of a different scale or the '1.0' scale.
This is useful information to list before you make your animation so that you can resize your character to match the scale
and have thing better align in-game. Note that this prints the *current* scale
so that means if you have the scale being modified by something else like one of the slider mods,
it could be printing the values from that instead of the vanilla values.
These are not bone scales, but rather the transform scales applied above the armature level.

For best results when playing an animation, try to hold your character still (don't hit extra buttons)
and perform the animation on flat ground and get the characters close to each other.
If an actor other than the player character is frozen when attempting the animation,
it may be because they are out of view in their original position.
Some advice for making the animation(s) is to try and avoid moving the root bone higher or lower.
This will not be 1:1 with the game. It is probably best to just leave the root bone alone in your animation
and if you need to offset it forwards/backwards/left/right while making your animations, set back at the end after finishing your animation(s).

JSON parsing structure for Extra Layered Armor:
'BodyArmorName' is used to specify which armor the custom armor is layering to.
'BodyArmorMeshPath', 'BodyArmorMaterialPath', 'BodyArmorAltMaterialPath',
'BodyArmorChainPath', 'BodyArmorAltChainPath', 'BodyArmorClspPath', 'BodyArmorGpucPath',
'BodyArmorJcnsPath' (This has a special parsing structure.
You can use as many Jcns files as you want, just be sure to include a suffix for each individual entry.
(example: 'BodyArmorJcnsPath1', 'BodyArmorJcnsPath2')
The value for these entries also have a special parsing structure.
An example being 'MyArmorMod\JointConstraintsFile.jcns(true)((2))(((1.0)))'
This can be broken down into path (string), enable update timing override (boolean),
update timing mode (int between 0-3), blend rate (System.Single).
More info for what these are set to is displayed within the ELA information.
'BodyArmorChainCollisionTarget', 'BodyArmorAltChainCollisionTarget' (enum) 0 = None, 1 = Extern, 2 = All
'BodyArmorGpucCollisionTarget' (enum) 0 = None, 1 = Extern, 2 = All, 3 = Max
'BodyArmorCustomLabelsID' (string with custom ID, these can be set the same as 'ArmorName' inside parts enable
and custom bone label json to match the identifiers and use custom labels).
These are also used for currently equipped display
labels if set to view them from ELA Settings.
These can all be set the same for other parts except
replace the Body prefix with Arm, Leg, Waist, Slinger or Helm.
Slinger doesn't have the word 'Armor' in it for the keys.
'HelmArmorEnableHairJointAdjustment' controls wether the hair joints are scaled/adjusted for helms.
This is what is being done sometimes when parts of the hair don't stick through helms.
'HelmHairAdjustList' (AdjustListPreset), paste in your helm hair adjust preset as the value.
It is meant for joint parameters and hair adjustment for the helm.
'HelmArmorDisableHair' (boolean value), fully enable/disable the hair.
'HelmArmorDisableHairOtherParts' (boolean value), fully disable the hair or hair other parts, sometimes used with specific armors.
'HelmArmorDisableEyebrows' (boolean value), fully enable/disable the eyebrows.
'HelmArmorDisableEyelashes' (boolean value), fully enable/disable eyelashes.
'HelmArmorEarObjScale' (System.Single), adjusts character ears scale.
'HelmArmorBackHeadObjScale' (System.Single), adjusts the scale of the back of the character's head.
'HelmArmorHeadObjScale' (System.Single), adjusts the scale of the character's head.
'ArmArmorDisableSlinger' (boolean value), and 'WaistArmorHideLight' (boolean value).
The alt chains can be used to swap to a secondary chain depending on how parts enabled are set.
This is useful if you have something like a bra holding some tits, and you remove it with parts enabled,
the tits would naturally sway more, hence swapping the chain.
You don't have to specify in JSON for things you don't use.
Or you can just set the value as 'nil' and that will also skip over/not use
a certain parameter like if you didn't want to set GPUC for example.
Paths are relative to natives\STM.
ELA data goes in reframework/data/FBSStartupData/ExtraLayeredArmor/*WhateverName*.json.

to armor pigmentation color to an external file

affect ONLY the vanilla armor(s) that ELA is being used with.

what is selected with the combo boxes.

the same chains/materials multiple times for them.

Parts Enabled that are set to invisible/unchecked and marked with
'(False for ELA Alt Chain Usage)' use specified alternate chain files for extra
layered armor. This is useful if, for example, you had hard metal plate
covering boobs and then wanted to remove the plate. Obviously
there would be a difference in jiggle hence why disabling
a part specified can automatically swap chain files.

Parts Enabled that are set to invisible/unchecked and marked with
'(False for ELA Alt Chain Usage)' use specified alternate chain files for extra
layered armor. This is useful if, for example, you had hard metal plate covering
boobs and then wanted to remove the plate. Obviously there would
be a difference in jiggle hence why disabling a part specified can automatically
swap chain files.

Parts Enabled that are set to invisible/unchecked and marked with
'(False for ELA Alt Chain Usage)' use specified alternate chain files for extra
layered armor. This is useful if, for example, you had hard metal plate covering
boobs and then wanted to remove the plate. Obviously there would be a
difference in jiggle hence why disabling a part specified can automatically
swap chain files.

Parts Enabled that are set to invisible/unchecked and marked with
'(False for ELA Alt Chain Usage)' use specified alternate chain files for extra layered armor.
This is useful if, for example, you had pants covering your character's butt
and then wanted to remove them.
Obviously there would be a difference in jiggle hence why disabling
a part specified can automatically swap chain files.

Parts Enabled that are set to invisible/unchecked and marked with
'(False for ELA Alt Chain and CLSP Usage)' use specified alternate chain or clsp files for extra
layered armor. This is useful for chain if, for example, you had hard metal plate
covering boobs and then wanted to remove the plate. Obviously there
would be a difference in jiggle hence why disabling
a part specified can automatically swap chain files.
This is useful for clsp to provide different collision sizes based on parts being enabled/disabled.
If you do not specify an alternate chain/clsp, they will not be used and the originals will be.
They also work independently, so you don't need both chain and clsp for it to work.

Parts Enabled that are set to invisible/unchecked and marked with
'(False for ELA Alt Chain and CLSP Usage)' use specified alternate chain or clsp files for extra layered armor.
This is useful for chain if, for example, you had pants covering your character's butt
and then wanted to remove them.
Obviously there would be a difference in jiggle hence why disabling
a part specified can automatically swap chain files.
This is useful for clsp to provide different collision sizes based on parts being enabled/disabled.
If you do not specify an alternate chain/clsp, they will not be used and the originals will be.
They also work independently, so you don't need both chain and clsp for it to work.

Parts Enabled that are set to invisible/unchecked and marked with
'(False for EO Alt Chain Usage)' use specified alternate chain files for extra outfits.
There are secondary and tertiary alternate chains to swap.
This useful for a combination such as
Chain1 = Bra + Pants, Chain2 = No Bra + Pants, Chain3 = Bra + No Pants, Chain4 = No Bra + No Pants;
to compensate for more realistic variances in jiggle.
More info in the Extra Outfits section on that.

Avoid changing scenes or equipment while actively editing colliders.
Doing so may cause the editor UI to become desynchronized from the current collider values.
Reopen/restart the editor if the displayed values no longer match the colliders.
Physics types supported for editing: Chain2, Clsp, and Gpuc.
Armors that do not make use of these will not show editors for whichever one(s) are not in use.
Symmetry is applied when a value changes after the setting has been enabled.
Existing values (that are potentially asymmetrical) are left unchanged.
The notes section is for anything you might want to add as a note in your preset.
For example, 'this preset is inteded to be used with this specific clsp file asset' or something like that.
Keep in mind that same edited values can still produce a different visual result depending on how the file asset is set up.
For example an offset value can change the look depending on the starting value.
An absolute value adjustment can change depending on the order of its attributes
or if previous absolute value saved data is applied.

dictionary_refs.key:
(Default=ON) Internal denoiser. When turned off, reflections
become clearer, and with some RT improvement if RT quality
is set to the highest. However, you may encounter
a flickering issue when moving between zones.

Applies a better shadow filtering method, resulting in smoother
and more accurate shadows.

The improvement is most noticeable in outdoor environments.

Controls the overall fidelity/filtering of shadows
(softness, accuracy, cascade quality).

Controls which surfaces receive RT reflections based on their
roughness value.

Diffuse GI ray tracing buffer resolution preset.
Origin_Res renders GI at full resolution.
Half_Res renders at half resolution and upsamples.
Doesn't seem to do anything for this game.

Disables LOD (Level of Detail) switching in the renderer.
All objects render at their highest available mesh detail
regardless of camera distance.

May improve geometry quality up close but impact is not fully
tested — could increase GPU load in dense areas.

Disables culling of entire objects whose screen-space projected
size falls below the threshold set by SmallObjectCullingRatio.

More aggressive than per-triangle culling — entire draw calls
are skipped when enabled. Disabling it forces all small distant
objects to render, reducing pop-in at a GPU geometry cost.

Enables dynamic shadow movement for trees, allowing their shadows
to sway naturally.

Disabling this will result in static, motionless tree shadows.

Maximum distance for specular/reflection RT rays.
Higher = reflections pick up geometry further away.

Maximum world-space distance a diffuse GI ray can travel.
Higher values allow GI to sample more distant geometry.

Scales the intensity of diffuse GI bounced light.
Higher = brighter indirect lighting.

Scales the intensity of specular/reflection bounced light.
Higher = brighter reflections.

Second bounce for specular/reflections. Only
works when denoiser is disabled.

Specular/reflection buffer resolution.
Origin_Res = sharper reflections at higher cost.
Half_Res = cheaper but softer reflections.
Leave unchecked to use the game default.

The texture resolution of shadow maps.
Higher = sharper shadows, but costs a lot of VRAM.

Toggles the entire post-processing stack (bloom, tone mapping,
color grading, lens effects, etc.).
Disabling it makes the image look very raw.

When ON the game increases the contribution of temporal RT history
(stronger accumulation), reducing noise faster and stabilising
static views — but can cause ghosting/trailing on fast motion
or rapid camera pans.

Disabling it reduces smearing around moving silhouettes and
props in dim scenes at the cost of more noise.

Whether RT rays respect alpha-tested geometry
(foliage, fences, hair).

Which lights are targeted by RT calculations
(dynamic scene lights, baked lights, or both).
